account:
Today has mostly looked like ordinary town business. I read my appointments, returned the book, and the secretary is helping me keep my schedule. The builder came to arrange repairs but repeatedly wanted a scope and payment agreement. I have authorized only an inspection and estimate, not spending; I have no confirmed damaged structures yet. That persistence is noticeable, but not proof of anything improper.

At the market, several residents reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery. I then saw the baker carrying a sack of bread and stocking the stall chest. Those observations fit normal bread production and sales; I have no evidence of a shortage or secret purpose.

The most unusual lead is that at about 10:53 I heard Townsfolk 03 and 23 both say, 'bridge or port change at inn.' I do not know what change they mean, who proposed it, or whether it is even accurate. It might concern transport or trade, but that is only a possibility. Freight is now nearby carrying an emerald; I have not observed any connection between freight and that report. I asked the baker about the remark and am awaiting an answer. I should seek the original witnesses' details rather than treat repeated wording as independent confirmation. My noon lunch at home and one o'clock accounts appointment remain ahead.
